tasks.title: Section A: Plastic pollution in oceans
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure A1 provides information on ocean gyres in the world. Resource Booklet Figure A2 shows the plastic waste emitted to the ocean per capita by country in 2019. Resource Booklet Figure A3 shows the share of global plastic waste emitted to the ocean by country in 2019.

parts.question: Name the natural resource from which most plastics are produced.
parts.reference: Suggested answers (award one of the answers listed): Fossil fuels, Crude oil, Petroleum, Natural gas. Award 1 mark for a correct answer. Accept any other relevant and complete answer.

parts.question: Identify two sources used to produce bioplastics.
parts.reference: Suggested answers (award two of the answers listed): Renewable biomass sources, Vegetable fats, Vegetable oils, Corn starch, Proteins, Sugar, Cellulose (straw, woodchips, sawdust), Rubber trees, Recycled food waste. Award 1 mark for each correct answer. Award a maximum of 2 listed sources. Accept any other relevant and complete answer.

parts.question: Choose one of the ocean gyres. Draw and label a diagram to show the wind patterns and ocean currents that contribute to the formation of your chosen gyre in the space below.
parts.reference: The sketch must show a selected ocean gyre in a complete environment of winds and ocean currents with the surrounding continents. It must include the following: The ocean gyre is shown in a specific area with surrounding continents outlined; Location and movement/directions of wind patterns for the selected location; Labelled trade winds and westerlies; Location and movement/direction of ocean currents for the selected location; Cold and warm currents drawn in different ways (colours, lines…). Award 5 marks for the map – 1 mark for each of the following key elements drawn on the map: setting of continents and ocean(s) for the selected location; location and direction/movement of winds from the air pressure maximum on selected location; labelled trade winds and westerlies; location and direction/movement of ocean currents for the selected location; cold and warm ocean currents labelled in a different way. Award 0.5 mark for each partially marked element on the map.

parts.question: Explain the reasons for the accumulation of plastic pollution in the location you have chosen.
parts.reference: Suggested answer: The circular nature of ocean currents (convergence) formed by global wind patterns and forces created by Earth’s rotation (Coriolis effect) then move the plastic (and other garbage) into ocean gyres; Poor management of plastic disposal on land leads to run-off into rivers which empty into oceans. Award 2 marks for a complete answer that includes an explanation of both accumulation of plastic waste into ocean gyres and production and discharge of plastic waste into oceans. Award 1 mark for a complete explanation of the accumulation of the plastic waste in oceans that includes two key elements. Award 0.5 mark for an incomplete explanation of the accumulation of the plastic waste in oceans that includes one key element. Award 1 mark for a complete explanation of the production and discharge of the plastic waste that includes two key elements. Award 0.5 mark for an incomplete explanation of the production and discharge of the plastic waste that includes one key element.

parts.question: Describe two spatial patterns regarding the origin of plastic waste emissions into the oceans. Provide specific data from the sources. Your answer should refer to regions and/or multiple countries, not individual countries.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Countries with a high percentage of plastic emissions do not necessarily have a high per capita of emissions (the larger percentage of plastic emissions is due to high human populations – e.g. India, China); Brazil, Philippines, Indonesia are high in per capita and percentage of plastic emissions; Many of the highest emitters are in LDCs or developing economies; The highest emitters are in SE Asia; Most of the highest emitters are countries on a sea or ocean or with large river systems; The highest emitters have limited efficient garbage handling systems and open landfills; Countries with a smaller geographical area, longer coastlines, high rainfall, and poor waste management systems are more likely to wash plastics into the sea. Award 2 marks for two described spatial patterns. Award 1 mark for each pattern with a reference to data from sources. Award 0.5 mark for each pattern without reference to data from sources.

parts.question: Using the sources provided and your geographical knowledge discuss why it is difficult to eliminate plastic pollution from entering the oceans. Give at least three arguments.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Plastics continue to be produced and used all over the world. The demand for plastics remains high; Much of the plastic pollution is discarded on land, then ends up in rivers or landfill sites and from there into the oceans – a ban on the use of plastic in every country would reduce this problem; Better waste management on land would help reduce the amount of plastic that ends up in the oceans; There is a global trade in plastic products and waste to places where there is insufficient infrastructure for safe and environmentally sound management; Incineration in combined heat and power plants, recycling, upcycling and downcycling are limited in their use and have restrictions or negative impacts; In many countries, plastic pollution is not a high priority for the government or citizens, so no action is taken; Lack of political will; Limited enforcement of existing laws; International nature of the problem – there are few treaties that are not honoured; Out of sight out of mind – the marine areas heavily affected by plastic pollution are far away from the sources of pollution and are not seen by people on a daily basis. Award 3 marks for three elaborated arguments. Award 1 mark for each elaborated argument that includes students’ knowledge and refers to sources. Award 0.5 mark for each argument that includes students’ knowledge or refers to sources.

tasks.title: Section B: Amazon rainforest ecosystem
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure B1 shows an overview of tropical forest degradation processes in the Amazon. Resource Booklet Figure B2 shows the distribution of PM2.5 persistent organic pollutants in the atmosphere in the Amazon Forest. Resource Booklet Figure B3 shows the extent of deforestation in the Amazon Forest.

parts.question: Identify and explain three main reasons for the deforestation of the Amazon rainforest.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Agriculture – clearing large areas of forest to get arable land to grow tropical cultures, particularly soy beans; Cattle ranching – large areas of forest are cleared to make way cattle raising, particularly to produce beef; Selective logging – for commercial purposes. Trees are cut down for timber used in furniture, paper, and other products; Mining – the demand for minerals like gold and iron ore drives mining in the Amazon. Mining activities are causing widespread destruction to the rainforest, including water pollution and soil degradation; Human activity (human settlements and infrastructure) – building settlements on the edge of rainforest increases the human pressure. Infrastructure development, such as roads, dams, and hydropower projects, is also contributing to deforestation; Fire – often caused by agricultural practices but can be exacerbated by extreme droughts; Extreme droughts – become increasingly frequent in the Amazon as land-use change and human-induced climate change progress, affecting tree mortality, fire incidence, and carbon emissions to the atmosphere; Lack of governance / corruption; Population growth. Award 3 marks for three identified and explained reasons. Award 1 mark for each identified and explained reason. Award 0.5 mark for each identified reason without an explanation.

parts.question: Analyse the spatial relationship between the intensity of PM 2.5 emissions and the extent of deforestation.
parts.reference: Suggested answer: The intensity of PM 2.5 emissions is generally positively correlated with the extent of deforestation; In the south-eastern part of the Amazon region, for example, the highest PM 2.5 emissions (> 0.02) are concentrated in the areas with the greatest deforestation (105 km2). The situation is similar in the south-western part of the Amazon, where the lowest concentration of PM 2.5 emissions coincides with the least deforestation; The cause of the above relationship is forest fire, which causes more PM to be released into the atmosphere and increases the PM concentration in the area of deforestation; On the other hand, areas with a low deforestation rate have a mean PM concentration that is higher than it should be. This could be due to the wind factor, which flows from east to west and brings the particulate matter with it. As a result, some areas with high deforestation in the east do not have high PM levels, while some areas in the centre have higher PM levels without significant deforestation. Award 3 marks for three completely analysed elements. Award 1 mark for each completely analysed element. Award 0.5 mark for each partially analysed element.

parts.question: What is meant by the term ecosystem services?
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Direct and indirect contributions of ecosystems (known as natural capital) for human well-being and quality of life; The various benefits that humans derive from healthy ecosystems. Award 0.5 mark for a complete answer.

parts.question: Identify and explain the importance of three ecosystem services provided by the Amazon rainforest.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Climate regulation; Carbon storage; Biodiversity support; Water regulation; Nutrient cycle. Award 4.5 marks for three identified and explained ecosystem services. Award 1.5 marks for each identified and completely explained ecosystem service: Award 0.5 mark for each identified ecosystem service; Award 1 mark for each completely explained ecosystem service; Award 0.5 mark for a partially explained ecosystem service.

parts.question: Specify two impacts of deforestation of the Amazon rainforest on its ecosystem services and two impacts on human well-being.
parts.reference: Suggested answers include impacts on climate regulation, carbon cycle, water cycle, human livelihoods, respiratory health, biodiversity loss. Award 2 marks for impacts of deforestation on ecosystem services and 2 marks for impacts on well-being. Award 1 mark for each completely specified impact. Award 0.5 mark for each partially specified impact. Do not award just giving a list of impacts without an explanation.

tasks.title: Section C: Monsoon and weather phenomena in Dubai
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Table C1 provides climate data of Kathmandu and Dubai. Resource Booklet Figure C1 shows Monsoon system mechanism in Indian ocean and surrounding continents. Resource Booklet Text Box C1 gives information on the flood after a rainstorm in Dubai on 19 April 2024. Resource Booklet Figure C2 shows satellite images before and during the deluge in the United Arab Emirates in April 2024. Resource Booklet Figure C3 shows flooded road and airport after a rainstorm in Dubai on 19 April 2024.

parts.question: Create a combined climate diagram that compares the precipitation and temperature data for both Dubai and Kathmandu in one diagram. Label your diagram appropriately.
parts.reference: Award 2 marks for appropriate climate diagram that displays data of both climates on the same, combined axis. Award 3 marks for the following elements – 0.5 marks for each of the following elements that have been drawn correctly: suitable title, labels on the axes, expressing Kathmandu and Dubai's data differently and intuitively, clear legend.

parts.question: Calculate the average annual temperature amplitude/range in Dubai and Kathmandu (round the value to one decimal place).
parts.reference: Answers: Dubai: 16.3°C; Kathmandu: 11.3°C. The temperature amplitude must be calculated from the table data with maximum accuracy to one decimal place. Award 1 mark for both correct values. Award 0.5 mark for each correct value.

parts.question: Explain the differences between the rainfall patterns in Dubai and Kathmandu, although both climates are influenced by the same wind patterns.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Dubai – dryness, monsoon winds mainly pass over continents with minimal contact with open water, winter westernly disturbances, lower temperatures in winter, terrain (Hajar Mountains), topography. Kathmandu – typical Asian monsoon bringing warm, moist air from the Indian Ocean, orographic effect and Himalayan barrier. Award 2 marks for the explanation of climate in Dubai and 2 marks for Kathmandu using level marking.

parts.question: Name one such primary atmospheric mechanism that can cause such conditions that lead to severe flooding.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Low-pressure systems (cyclones, depression…), Frontal systems (cold weather fronts), Jet streams, La Niña + Negative IOD (Indian Ocean Dipole). Award 1 mark for one of listed answers.

parts.question: Explain two reasons why, even after significant rain events, the landscape in Dubai remains arid and the surrounding desert does not transform into a green environment.
parts.reference: Main reasons: Desert soil properties and lack of ground cover; High evaporation rates. Additional reasons: Infrequency of rain; Adaptation of local vegetation. Award 2 marks for two explained reasons. Award 1 mark for each completely explained reason.

parts.question: Discuss how the urban environment of Dubai contributed to the flooding in April 2024.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Urban environment has extensive development and increased impermeable surfaces such as roads, buildings, and pavements; These surfaces prevent water from naturally infiltrating into the ground, leading to higher runoff during rainfall; The lack of suitable drainage systems to cope with sudden, intense rainfall exacerbates the situation. Award 2 marks for a complete answer including at least two explained arguments.

tasks.title: Section D: Periglacial landscape and climate change
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure D1 shows the map of permafrost zones in the Arctic area. Resource Booklet Figure D2 shows satellite images of the site on Taymyr Island in Russian Siberia in July 1966 and July 2009. Resource Booklet Table D1 gives data on main greenhouse gasses in the atmosphere. Resource Booklet Figure D3 shows the contribution of greenhouse gases to global temperature rise (2010-2019 compared to 1850-1900).

parts.question: Identify the area near the North Pole where there are no or only a few isolated permafrost areas.
parts.reference: Answer: Iceland; Spitzberger (Svalbard). Award 1 mark for the correct answer.

parts.question: Suggest the reason why this area is free of permafrost.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Warm ocean currents, Gulf stream, Norwegian warm current (North Atlantic Current), Stream drift. Award 1 mark for a complete answer that includes warm ocean currents and the exact name of the current.

parts.question: With the help of information provided and your geographical understanding outline two reasons why the extent of permafrost areas in North America differs significantly from that in Europe.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Small relative distance to the sea; Warm ocean currents that reach northernmost Europe; Wet and dry landscapes; Thickness of soil layers; Vegetation or lack of vegetation; Permafrost needs landmasses to develop. Award 2 marks for two outlined reasons.

parts.question: Describe the change in the vegetation from 1966 to 2009.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: The vegetation has been getting both taller and expanding in space and range; The vegetation is much denser in 2009, with almost no areas without forest; Areas with tundra are being replaced by coniferous forests (taiga). Award 1 mark for any of suggested answers.

parts.question: Explain how climate change has affected the described change in vegetation.
parts.reference: Suggested answer: Growing temperatures cause snow and ice to melt earlier in spring; Warming of the tundra climate enables growing taller and denser forest vegetation; Warming of the Arctic Ocean enables increasing temperature on surrounding land; Permafrost changes (active layer becomes thicker due to thawing). Award 2 marks for a complete answer.

parts.question: Outline the mechanism by which this change in vegetation can affect the climate.
parts.reference: Suggested answer: As shrubbery increases its distribution, it creates its own warming effect by absorbing heat rather than reflecting heat as snow does (changing albedo), leading to additional warming. Award 1 mark for a complete answer.

parts.question: Analyse the change in the concentrations of carbon dioxide and methane in the atmosphere from pre-industrial times to the present day and their contribution to the rise in temperature. Use statistical data to justify your answers.
parts.reference: Suggested answers for concentrations: CO2 increased from 278 ppm to 416 ppm (47.5%); CH4 increased from 729 to 1908 ppb (161.7%). Contribution to temperature rise: CO2 is responsible for 0.7-0.8°C and methane for 0.5°C. Award 1 mark for change in concentrations with statistical indicators and 1 mark for temperature contributions.

parts.question: Evaluate the role of carbon dioxide and methane in global warming. Justify your answer with specific data.
parts.reference: Point marking – award 4 marks for a complete answer that contains: explanation of effects on climate (GWP); atmospheric lifetime; comparison of concentration and growth rate; comparison of the two gases; statistical data. Level marking – evaluation of short- and long-term effects (1 mark).

tasks.title: Section E: Olympic Games
tasks.statement: The Olympic Games are a global event that attracts attention worldwide. They bring athletes, tourists, politicians and others together to create a global spectacle and leave a certain legacy. Resource Booklet Figure E1 shows the population and number of participants in London Summer Olympic Games in 2012 per continent. Resource Booklet Figure E2 represents the ranking of Olympic cities according to ecological, social and economic sustainability. Resource Booklet Figure E3 shows the aerial imagery of the site of the Olympic Village of Poblenou in Barcelona in 1977 and in 2022. Resource Booklet Figure E4 gives an insight into the Barcelona urban regeneration project 1986-1992. Resource Booklet Figure E5 shows the condition of one of the venues after the Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro.

parts.question: Name the continent that was most underrepresented at the London Olympics when comparing the ratio of Olympic participants to the world's population. Justify your answer with specific data.
parts.reference: Answer: Asia. Justification data: 0.5 athlete per 1 million people / 1 athlete per 2 million people / 19.0% of participants compared to 60.7% of population. Award 1 mark for the name of the continent and for the evidence.

parts.question: Describe the general trend of the overall sustainability of the Olympic Games 1992-2020. Your answer should not include only one aspect (pillar) of sustainability.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Sustainability is not evaluated as high; overall sustainability has decreased over time; economic sustainability generally has an increasing trend while ecological dimension declines the most; Summer and Winter Olympics have similar overall sustainability; Winter Games fluctuate more. Award a maximum of 2 marks (0.5 mark for each described element).

parts.question: Suggest two main reasons for the described trend.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: None of the games achieved a high level of sustainability in all three dimensions; major investments, large facilities construction, relocation of people, corruption, high costs, social insecurity; new construction and social safety receive poor ratings; long-term viability has relatively strong record; differences between host cities/countries; promotion of environment as a pillar has not stopped the decline. Award a maximum of 2 marks for explained reasons.

parts.question: Analyse the process of urban transformation of Barcelona between 1977 and the time of the 1992 Summer Olympics (in terms of general character, services, size/locations).
parts.reference: Suggested answer: Before transformation, waterfront was inaccessible and consisted of run-down industry; redevelopment project covered coastal area and included completely transformed neighborhoods, ring roads, new airport, improved public transport, green spaces; construction of new sports facilities and new Olympic Village in Poblenou. Award 3 marks for three outlined/explained elements.

parts.question: Explain two ways in which the urban remodelling of Barcelona has improved the quality of life of its citizens.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: City parks and green areas (Montjuïc Park); beaches and coastal promenade (4 km promenade with imported sand); leisure and amusement services; new living spaces (converted athlete housing); ring roads and airport; new sports facilities. Award 2 marks for two fully explained impacts.

parts.question: Evaluate whether major sporting events such as the Olympic Games have a positive or negative socio-economic impact on the target cities during and after these events. Use at least two positive and two negative socio-economic impacts as examples to support your ideas.
parts.reference: A complete answer must include: two positive socio-economic impacts – point marking – 2 marks (1 mark for each); two negative socio-economic impacts – point marking – 2 marks (1 mark for each); final evaluation – level marking – 1 mark.

tasks.title: Section F: Commuting mobility in the cities
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure F1 shows the map of the most frequent mode of transport for selected World cities. Each dot represents a city. The size of each dot is proportional to the population of the city. Resource Booklet Figure F2 shows ABC modal share for selected 794 World cities. The size of the disc is proportional to the city’s population, and the colour corresponds to the region.

parts.question: Identify the most frequently used transport modes for commuters in cities in North America and Europe.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: North America: cars are dominant in commuting mobility in all selected cities. Europe: cars dominant but high share of selected cities also has active mobility as a dominant transport mode; public transport more present in Eastern and Western Europe. Award 1 mark for correct answer for North America and 1 mark for correct answer for Europe.

parts.question: Give two differences between the way commuters travel in Tokyo and Dhaka. Explain three reasons for these differences.
parts.reference: Suggested answers - Differences (2 marks): similar percentage of cars (~13-14%); ~50% of commuters in Tokyo use public transport compared to ~29% in Dhaka; active mobility is ~35% in Tokyo and ~57% in Dhaka. Reasons (3 marks): Tokyo has higher income and better quality public transport; Tokyo commuters travel longer distances; Dhaka faces severe traffic jams and poorer quality public transport infrastructure. Award 2 marks for differences and 3 marks for reasons.

parts.question: Explain the negative aspects of the increase in commuting on people and the economy.
parts.reference: Suggested answers - People (2 marks): increased stress levels and anxiety, impact on health (lower physical activity, high blood pressure, back pain), social isolation. Economy (2 marks): cost of commuting (fuel, parking, tolls, tickets), reduced productivity of commuters affecting economic growth. Award 2 marks for people and 2 marks for economy.

parts.question: To ensure efficient and sustainable commuting, public policymakers face many challenges. Suggest 4 possible solutions that policymakers may adopt to achieve this goal.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Solution 1: Encouraging alternative modes of transportation (bicycles, public transit, carpooling); Solution 2: Investing in transportation infrastructure (roads, highways, public transit systems); Solution 3: Implementing congestion pricing (charges for driving in congested areas during peak hours); Solution 4: Encouraging telecommuting (working from home). Award 4 marks for four proposed solutions (1 mark for each).
